messages:
jordan: thinking about adding per-entity rate limiting for SLO notifications (per-tenant / per-route) to reduce noise. quick sketch:

jordan: - allow configs: max_notifications_per_minute, sampling_window, suppression_mode (drop/summarize)

caroline: +1. Need console surface to show suppressed count and last-suppressed examples. ops keep asking 'what got suppressed?'

mike: we also need telemetry: metric `slo_notify.suppressed_total{entity,reason}` + `slo_notify.suppression_latency_ms` to see backlog

jordan: good call. For routing: when limit hit, do we fallback to lower-priority notification channels (email->ticket) or suppress entirely?

dana: prefer fallback chain: push -> email -> ticket. But for rate-limited tenants we should honor emergency rules (severity=critical always bypasses)

sam: how will API look for operators? maybe POST /api/v1/notify-configs/{entity} with body ```{
  "max_per_min": 5,
  "mode": "summarize",
  "fallback_chain": ["push","email"]
}```

caroline: console -> UX: show per-entity quota usage graph, remaining tokens, and a 'peek' of suppressed alerts with 'replay' button :eyes:

mike: implement server-side token bucket per-entity. But we already have global notifier throughput. Need isolation so a noisy tenant doesn't starve others.

jordan: agree. token buckets + shared backpressure pool for burst capacity. Also add per-route weights so high-impact SLOs get preferential tokens.

sam: what about sampling? If mode=summarize we should keep 1 in N sampled notifications to keep a trace per window (configurable sampler)

dana: and record `slo_notify.suppressed_reason` dimension (rate_limit, dedupe, downstream_error) so we can build alerts for suppression spikes

mike: edgecases: canary rollout — start with 1% of tenants, flag `slo_rate_limit_v2` and a runtime list. Need metrics for canary: suppressed_ratio_by_tenant

caroline: console needs a view to run adhoc "resend suppressed" for a tenant for a given time range (audit use)

alert-bot: Deploy pipeline note: `notifier-service` change requires schema migration: add `suppressed_count` column to notifications table (backfill = 0) :robot_face:

jordan: good point. Also contract debate: Should internal API return 429 for suppressed notifications, or return 200 with `suppressed:true`? Which is easier for downstream services?

sam: prefer 200 + metadata (`suppressed:true, reason:rate_limit`) so callers can log and continue. 429 will cascade.

dana: agree. Put in RFC: `POST /v1/notify` returns {"status":"accepted|suppressed","reason":...}

mike: perf note: when summarizing, create a single aggregated notification with count and sample traces. keep ordering of alerts though.

caroline: UX detail: show 'suppression policy' on SLO edit screen with a little tooltip explaining default values and cost impacts :chart_with_upwards_trend:

jordan: next steps: - draft API shape (sam) - notifier service design doc (mike) - console mockups (caroline) - telemetry dashboard (dana)

sam: I'll start API PR. tag me for reviews @mike

caroline: I'll put mockups in figma and drop link when ready

mike: I'll write design doc and include load testing plan

dana: adding telemetry checklists to backlog. also add alert if suppressed_ratio > 0.2 for >1h

jordan: thanks all. rolling this into next sprint planning. :thumbsup:
